primitives.note: Passive converts bonus health into bonus AD (1 bonus AD per 14 bonus health), which feeds the bonus-AD ratios on Q, E, and R.
Q channels for up to 3s (or a 0.4-0.5s quick-release) before its recast fires; Pyke is slowed/limited during the charge and then locked out while the harpoon is in flight.
Q's damage only happens on the recast (quick-release thrust or empowered harpoon) after the initial charge cast; R can be recast for free within 20s if it kills a champion inside the X.
Mana costs (70-90 for Q, 40 for E, 100 for R) can limit how many casts fit in a 15s window depending on mana pool/regen from the build.
E's damage/stun resolves on a fixed 1s delay after cast (when the phantom returns), then goes on cooldown.
R deals a much larger 'raw' amount if the target is below a level-scaling health threshold (executed) versus a fixed 50% physical amount if above it.

needsBespoke.why: Every damage-relevant mechanic (charged/recast Q, delayed E hit, execute-threshold R, passive stat conversion, mana costs) is expressible with the listed primitives; nothing requires bespoke logic beyond combining them.

options: Dummy HP never drops below the (high, level-scaling) threshold, so R always deals the reduced 50% physical amount
Dummy HP is tracked and can fall below the threshold late in the fight, triggering the full raw-damage execute and a free recast
Simulator ignores the execute branch entirely and always uses the non-execute physical formula
quotes: executing enemy {{tip|champions}} within the area that are below {{as|{{pp|250;290;330;370;400;430;450;470;490;510;530;540;550|6 to 18}}|health}}
Other enemies hit and enemy champions above the threshold are instead dealt 50% of the amount as physical damage.

unsettled.question: Should the simulated build be assumed to carry any Lethality, given P, W, E and R all have explicit per-Lethality scaling terms that are otherwise 0?
options: Assume 0 Lethality (pure AD/other build) so these ratios contribute nothing
Assume some nonzero Lethality since Pyke is commonly itemized with it, materially changing R's threshold/damage and E's stun duration

proposal: Do not cast W: it deals no damage and its camouflage/movement-speed benefits are ignored under the fight's mobility rule, so casting it only wastes mana and a GCD.
Open with a quick-release Q (tap, ~0.4s) at point-blank range on the dummy for its physical damage, since a full 3s charge only extends range, which is irrelevant against a stationary adjacent dummy.
Cast E (Phantom Undertow) through the dummy; its damage and stun resolve 1s later when the phantom returns, during which Pyke can keep auto-attacking.
Cast R (Death from Below) on the dummy for its large upfront physical damage (using the non-execute 50% formula, since the dummy is assumed to stay above the execute threshold for most of the fight).

Fill all remaining time with basic attacks, and recast Q and E again each time they come off cooldown (Q every 8-10s, E every 11-15s depending on rank), since Pyke has no onhit rider or attack-reset to change basic-attack value.
Only consider a free R recast if the dummy is actually brought below the execute threshold and dies inside the X during the cast, which likely does not occur before the 15s window ends.
questions: Is quick-releasing Q always strictly better for damage output than charging it, given the fight has no range requirement, or does charge time interact with cooldown/lockout in a way that changes optimal cast frequency?
Should R be cast immediately at the start of the fight for maximum early burst, or held later in case the dummy's HP is being tracked down toward the execute threshold?
Given R's long cooldown (70-100s), is more than one R cast ever expected within a single 15s fight, or should the rotation assume exactly one R cast?
Does the simulator model Pyke's own mana pool/regen enough that mana costs (Q 70-90, E 40, R 100) actually constrain how many Q/E casts fit into 15s, or is mana assumed unlimited for this fight?
